question: Does visual imagery preserve a stable perception<->imagery angular geometry while repeat-to-repeat calibration variability is dominated by continuous scale/reliability fluctuations rather than changes in that angular geometry?
conceptual_model: geometry = stable angular relation + continuous reliability variation (NOT discrete latent-state switching); x_{s,i,r}=mu_{s,i}+sqrt(lambda_{s,i,r}) Sigma_s^1/2 eps is a TESTED MODEL CLASS only; lambda is NOT a biological quantity

hypotheses.H1_angular_scaffold: is the perception<->imagery principal-angle signature reproducibly stable across imagery repeats beyond matched pipeline constraints?
hypotheses.H2_continuous_reliability: does a prospectively-defined Student-t scale/reliability score from training-side repeat geometry predict held-out M4T2 calibration performance?

part1_repeat_angle.M4T1_REPEAT_GEOMETRY: per subject/ROI/fold/balanced-M4-subset/repeat r: geometry from the 4 single-repeat imagery observations at position r (exact frozen machinery, no tuning)
part1_repeat_angle.A_r: X1 B_angles cos^2(theta) between frozen perception support col(W) and the repeat-specific imagery support (rank = min(K,4) from 4 single-repeat residuals)
part1_repeat_angle.A_-r: leave-one-repeat-out reference: same 4 identities, repeats {0..7}\{r}, frozen full-resource estimator; target repeat r excluded
part1_repeat_angle.D_ANGLE: ||A_r - A_-r||_2 after deterministic component normalization (lower = more stable)

part2_student_t_reliability.objective: test whether the continuous per-trial scale predicts O2.14 schedule quality (NOT rediscover Student-t wins)
part2_student_t_reliability.fit: frozen multivariate Student-t on identity-residualized D=2 OUTSIDE repeat geometry, TRAINING imagery only; held-out identities inaccessible
part2_student_t_reliability.leave_identity_out_scoring: fit reference on OTHER training identities, score identity i's repeats (no own-identity leakage)
part2_student_t_reliability.robust_weight: w=(nu+D)/(nu+d^2), D=2 (operationally 'continuous reliability weight' ONLY; not attention/noise/arousal/precision/physiology)
part2_student_t_reliability.REL_SCALE: mean(log w) over the 8 schedule observations (log frozen before outcomes; do NOT test min/max/median/harmonic/clipping)

scale_association.per_subject_roi_fold: Spearman(REL_SCALE, ROBUSTNESS_MARGIN) over all valid M4T2 schedules (schedules estimate, not inferential N)

scale_matched_null.within_subject_roi_fold_identity: permute repeat-position reliability weights preserving identity/values/repeat count/schedule/outcome
scale_matched_null.E_SCALE: Z_SCALE_real/mean(Z_SCALE_null) (positive => reliability predicts beyond repeat-label exchangeability)

primary_inference.family: EXACTLY 4 tests: ventral E_ANGLE, lateral E_ANGLE, ventral E_SCALE, lateral E_SCALE

H1_support: per ROI iff ALL: median E_ANGLE>0; >=6/8 E_ANGLE>0; Holm-reject in final 4-test family; pipeline-triviality guard passes
H2_support: per ROI (CONTINUOUS_SCALE_RELIABILITY_SUPPORTED) iff ALL: median E_SCALE>0; >=6/8 E_SCALE>0; median raw rho_SCALE>0; >=6/8 raw rho_SCALE>0; Holm reject

descriptive_diagnostics.angular_pair_disagreement: ||A_repeatA - A_repeatB|| per M4T2 pair vs margin (expect negative; no p)
descriptive_diagnostics.scale_vs_angle_dominance: DELTA_DOM=|rho_SCALE|-|rho_ANGLE| (descriptive; scale need NOT beat angle for PASS)
descriptive_diagnostics.high_low_reliability_angle: split repeats by median t-weight; ANGLE_HIGH/LOW vs leave-out reference (does X1 angle survive in low-reliability?)
descriptive_diagnostics.x1_loso_reliability_stratified: X1 donor-mean LOSO for B_angles on HIGH and LOW reliability separately; report sign of X1 shared-angle effect (no new p)
descriptive_diagnostics.repeat_position_residualized: subtract repeat-position mean log-weight; recompute scale association (persists=schedule-specific info beyond position; vanishes=position-explained)
descriptive_diagnostics.qout_scale: Spearman(REL_SCALE, sealed O2.15 Q_OUT) + rho(REL_SCALE,margin) vs rho(Q_OUT,margin) (complementary; no winner)
descriptive_diagnostics.cross_roi_reliability: ventral vs lateral nu / weights / REL_SCALE participant correlation (no inference; global-process consistent but source unidentified)
descriptive_diagnostics.continuous_tail: fitted nu, Mahalanobis distribution, weights, tail fraction below fixed descriptive quantiles (no new threshold, no bad-trial class)
descriptive_diagnostics.gaussian_vs_t_replay: certify Student-t>=Gaussian/K2 (frozen X2 models; no re-inference)

program_status.CONSERVED_ANGULAR_SCAFFOLD_WITH_CONTINUO: H1 both ROIs AND H2 both ROIs AND X1 B_angles nontrivial/shared AND X2 discrete negative AND Student-t premise valid
program_status.ANGULAR_SCAFFOLD_SUPPORTED_RELIABILITY_L: H1 both ROIs but H2 partial/negative
program_status.CONTINUOUS_RELIABILITY_LINK_SUPPORTED_AN: H2 both ROIs but H1 partial/negative

claim_boundaries.positive: within the discovery cohort, the perception-to-imagery principal-angle relationship remained more stable across repeated imagery measurements than matched constrained geometries, while a continuous Student-t reliability score derived entirely from training-side repeat geometry predicted held-out calibration success in both primary ROIs; together with failed direct orientation transfer and failed discrete-state modeling this is consistent with a stable angular scaffold expressed in subject-specific coordinates and perturbed by continuous repeat-level reliability variation
forbidden: Student-t is the biological generative process

pipeline_triviality_requirement: any angular-stability positive MUST beat matched constrained synthetic operators else H1 pipeline-trivial and cannot contribute to PASS
synthetic_controls: 1 fixed scaffold + t scale -> H1,H2 recover
2 random orientation + t scale -> H1 fails H2 may pass
3 stable angles + Gaussian homoscedastic -> H1 pass H2 null
4 discrete two-state -> scale not falsely unique
x2_adaptation_record: X2 used leave-one-training-identity-out because trial-level repeats for the 2 outer-held-out identities are not in sealed trial_native; X3 records this and uses ONLY genuinely existing repeat-level identity data (10 training identities x 8 repeats); any result bounded to that set

next_gate.FULL_SUPPORTED: X3-REPLICATION: add angular/reliability as SECONDARY preregistered endpoints to the future O2.16 independent cohort (do NOT alter O2.16 primary endpoints; do NOT optimize the same N=8)
next_gate.partial: freeze the supported component for future replication; no replacements
next_gate.negative: seal negative; no alternative distributions/features on this cohort
